biography: Leandro Totti's journey began amidst the vibrant chaos of São Paulo, where the roar of engines was as commonplace as samba rhythms. His father, a mechanic with a local karting team, introduced him to the sport at a tender age. Leandro's raw talent was evident from the start, tearing up the karting scene with a fearless, borderline reckless style. A defining moment came during the 2010 Brazilian Karting Championship, where he executed a daring last-lap overtake that secured him the title and caught the eye of Vulkan's junior program. After some initial success in formula cars, Leandro found his true calling in endurance racing, joining MetalMoro MRX Duratec Turbo P3 in 2018. Although he has yet to clinch a major championship, Leandro's blistering pace and relentless determination make him a constant threat on the track, and a driver to watch in the coming seasons.
drivingStyle: Totti's driving style is characterized by an unyielding aggression. He attacks corners with a late-braking technique, often pushing the car to its absolute limit. While this approach yields spectacular results, it also leads to occasional overshoots and tire wear issues. He thrives under pressure, often delivering his best performances when the stakes are highest. Tire management is a work in progress for Leandro, but he is quickly improving as his experience grows.
rivalries: Ricardo Silva: A long-standing rivalry stemming from their karting days, marked by numerous on-track collisions and off-track verbal spars.
Isabela Oliveira: A more recent rivalry fueled by intense battles for podium positions in the Brazilian endurance championship. Their contrasting driving styles often lead to thrilling encounters.
Kenji Tanaka: An international rivalry developed during a guest appearance race in Japan, after a post-race disagreement about on-track etiquette.
quirks: Always wears the same lucky socks, regardless of the weather.
Listens to a specific Brazilian samba song right before every race to calm his nerves.

famousQuote: "Racing isn't about finesse, it's about heart. You gotta go out there and take what's yours!"
careerHighlight: Winning the 2017 Interlagos 6 Hours with a daring final stint, overtaking two cars in the last lap to secure victory for MetalMoro.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the 2020 Brazilian Endurance Championship finale due to a mechanical failure, costing him the championship title.
